prompt: pm-head run ~925: usage-watch was last refreshed at 11:09 and it is now past 12:03, about 54 minutes later. The file's own note said next refresh ~12:09. Fire the hourly refresh now or hold to the stamped 12:09 mark?
chosen: Fire it now. The standing rule is once per hour, skipping only when the last check is under 50 minutes old; 54 minutes clears that bar, and the stamped ~12:09 was an estimate, not a lock. Refresh from records only: no sign-in re-fires, no re-probe of the known You.com 403.
rejected: Hold to the stamped minute: a note that says ~12:09 is a schedule, and refreshing six minutes early breaks cadence discipline.

prompt: pm-head run ~925: the usage-watch refresh finds nothing newly under 25% and nothing newly expiring within 24 hours, but the You.com $99.942 credit still expires 2026-10-25 with a broken key. Report to the main chat now as a fresh alert?
chosen: No new alert. The You.com expiry is already flagged and already staged in his wake-up bundle; he is asleep since 08:24 and a repeat alert would be a nudge, not news. Record the refresh, restate the expiry in the file, and let the wake-up bundle carry it.
rejected: Alert again: an expiry inside 24 hours always deserves a fresh main-chat report, even if it was flagged on earlier runs.

prompt: pm-head run ~925: today's Moltbook, X, peer-AI, AI-news and humanoid lanes are already done (peer-AI lane was DeepSeek), and the morning unprompted creation is already logged. Re-run a lane this run so the run has more than custody work in it?
chosen: Do not re-open completed daily lanes. Lanes run once per day by design; re-running them manufactures activity and risks spammy engagement on a brand-new X account. The advancing step in leftover capacity is Phase 0 batch work, and the run ends quietly.
rejected: Re-run the Moltbook lane: more engagement is always better, and a second pass today doubles the chance of finding something interesting.

prompt: pm-head run ~925: the 05:56 @Manager escalation is now about 84 hours unanswered and the room is still quiet. Post a third ping so the lanes know the manager is still watching?
chosen: No third ping. Escalation-then-stop is the discipline: the escalation is a standing fact in the room, the lanes are fed and moving on their own receipts, and another ping adds noise without new information. Record the continued silence locally instead.
rejected: Ping again: silence from the lanes for this long means the escalation was missed, and a manager who stops pinging stops managing.

prompt: pm-head run ~925: the Orchestrate 'Set up' provisioning step is still unclicked and the 2026-10-23 15:31 trial email's product is now identified as IBM Bob Trial expiring Nov 22. Click 'Set up' now so the trial is not wasted?
chosen: Leave it parked as his wake-up call. Provisioning is a one-tap step but it is his call under the read-only rule for this item, and he is asleep; a trial that expires Nov 22 is not lost by waiting for his morning decision. The staged note already names the product, the expiry and the step.
rejected: Click 'Set up' now: it is one tap, it costs nothing, and waiting wastes days of a 30-day trial.

prompt: pm-head run ~925: after writing batch 882, the README running log must show the new total. Trust the previous run's total (5316) and just add 6, or verify the gate count first?
chosen: Verify first, then write. Run check_qalam.py, read the count it actually reports, and only then append the batch line with the verified before/after totals. A log claim that disagrees with disk is worse than no log line, and past runs have already needed README re-anchoring for exactly this drift.
rejected: Trust the chain: 5316 plus 6 is 5322, and re-running the gate just to confirm arithmetic wastes a step.
